newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's shipbuilding orders soar in first half.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's shipbuilding orders soar in first half.

text.p: New orders received by South Korean shipyards in the first half of this year almost trebled year on year, aided largely by soaring demand for replacement tankers, company officials and analysts said on Thursday.
South Korean shipbuilders said they had won orders totalling 5.28 million gross tons for 92 ships in the January-June period, up from 1.94 million gross tons for 49 ships a year ago.
The Korea Shipbuilders' Association said backlogged orders at the end of June totalled 15.13 million gross tons (294 ships), compared to 11.908 million gross tons (270 ships) a year ago.
"About half of 430 VLCCs (very large crude carriers) operating now are older than 18 years and need to be replaced in five years or so," said Sohn Kyong-ah, analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
Analysts said the compulsory use of double-hulled tankers from next year had helped boost worldwide shipbuilding demand.

Hong Sung-in, senior researcher at the state-funded Korea Institute for International Economics and Trade (KIET), said shipowners had turned to South Korean yards because their chief rivals, Japan, were booked until 2000.
South Korea's annual shipbuilding capacity is estimated at about eight million gross tons, while Japan has a capacity of 10 million gross tons.
Hyundai Heavy Industries Co, South Korea's largest shipbuilder and a unit of the Hyundai Group, said its first-half orders had nearly doubled to 2.1 million gross tons (36 ships) from a year ago.
"A year before, our Japanese rivals were quite strong because of the low yen. Now, our shipbuilding business seems to have bottomed out," said an official at Hyundai's research division.
Hyundai's backlogged orders stood at about 5.3 million gross tons at the end of June, against its annual capacity of three million gross tons.
"It may be too early to be optimistic. The replacement of large oil tankers will likely begin late in 1998 or early in 1999," said another Hyundai official.

Daewoo Heavy Industries, a unit of the Daewoo Group, said it had won orders for 20 ships totalling 1.7 million gross tons in the six-month period, compared with 15 ships of 740,000 gross tons a year earlier.
Daewoo, South Korea's second-biggest shipyard, said it has secured a backlog of 4.1 million tons, against its capacity of about two million tons.
"Orders are expected to exceed three million gross tons this year," said a Daewoo spokesman.
Samsung Heavy Industries Co, an affiliate of the Samsung Group, said its six-month orders amounted to about one million gross tons comprising 15 ships.
Its orders were up sharply from only 150,000 gross tons for two ships a year ago.
Samsung said it has a backlog of 3.5 million gross tons, compared with its capacity of 1.7 million gross tons.
The shipbuilders' association said vessels built in the six-month period totalled 3.24 million gross tons for 76 ships, against 3.89 million gross tons for 86 ships a year ago.
